subject: reusable shopping bags
title: What If You Never Washed Your Shopping Bags?

scenes.text: What if you never washed your shopping bags? The danger isn't the dirt you can see.
Researchers swabbed 84 bags from real shoppers. About half carried coliform bacteria, and 12 percent had E. coli.
Why? About 97 percent of the shoppers they asked had never washed or bleached their bags.
Add meat juice, leave a bag in a warm car trunk for 2 hours, and bacteria grew about tenfold.
In 2010, one bag stored in a hotel bathroom spread a stomach virus through a girls' soccer team.
The fix is one wash, which cut the bacteria by more than 99 percent. The bag was never the problem.

description:
What if you never washed your shopping bags? A study of 84 reusable bags in Los Angeles, San Francisco and Tucson found coliform bacteria in about half and E. coli in 12%; 97% of shoppers said they had never washed them, and washing cut bacteria by more than 99% (Loma Linda University, TIME).
In 2010 a reusable bag kept in a hotel bathroom was linked to a norovirus outbreak on an Oregon girls' soccer team (CIDRAP, ScienceDaily).
